title: Show physical network behind TUN routes
head: 06fcdcd86e40
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: A valid multipath or nexthop-ID main default has no top-level dev, so the physical route is silently discarded
leads.consequence: For a main-table ECMP default such as {dst:default,nexthops:[{dev:eth0,gateway:10.0.1.1},{dev:eth1,gateway:10.0.2.1}]}, .dev is absent, nmcli is asked about an empty interface, and the loop never chooses either physical nexthop. It falls back to policy ip route get; behind a TUN the panel and plain status again show Meta/198.18.0.1, not the requested physical transport. The next poll repeats. A route with nhid and nexthop_compat_mode=0 has the same top-level absence. Explicitly resolve nexthops (or the nhid) before discarding a route.
leads.triage: already covered by Opus F6 (multipath falls back to probe route, same as merge base); not a regression; not published

leads.summary: The new no-prefsrc fallback chooses the first IPv4 address, not the route's effective source; the prefix can describe another address
leads.consequence: A route with no explicit prefsrc and multiple IPv4 addresses chooses addr_info[0] rather than the IPv4 source selected for this gateway (the kernel excludes secondary addresses and matches the gateway network). The panel's IP/copy action can show the wrong LAN address. Even when the main route has prefsrc, prefix is always read from the first address, so verbose can print ip 10.0.1.22 with prefix 25 belonging to 10.0.1.77, rather than /24. Repeated polling keeps showing the mismatch. Query the selected route's effective source and find the matching addr_info entry for the prefix; cover multiple/secondary addresses.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F4; confirmed with real kernel routes (opus run5); published as address-fallback finding

leads.summary: A link-down physical default remains selectable even if the kernel ignores that nexthop
leads.consequence: With ignore_routes_with_linkdown set and a lower-metric eth0 default flagged linkdown plus a usable eth1 default, the kernel refuses eth0 for lookup but the new route-list scan still picks it: nmcli GENERAL.TYPE says ethernet regardless of connected state, and flags, NM state and address presence are not tested. Panel reads eth0 counters and gateway instead of the working eth1 or the probe route; each 1.5-second sample repeats the error. Check route flags/NM state or verify the candidate can actually carry traffic before returning it.
leads.triage: behavioural; neutral Opus follow-up 1 confirmed with real kernel routes: head keeps dead linkdown route only when ignore_routes_with_linkdown=1, NM removes route ~6 s after carrier loss; published as one sentence in finding 1 suggested change

leads.summary: The reported physical router latency is not bound to the selected physical interface
leads.consequence: With policy routing sending even the selected main-route gateway through the TUN (or making it unreachable), `ping "$gateway"` obeys that policy rather than using `$iface`; router_ping_ms then measures the tunnel path or times out despite the displayed physical gateway. The internet ping remains against 1.1.1.1 through the policy path by design; those two measurements are no longer on the same interface as the visible counters and IP. The existing test's ping stub always answers, so it cannot catch this. Consider binding only the router probe to the displayed interface or clearly distinguishing physical link metrics from policy-path reachability.
leads.triage: behavioural; Opus follow-up 1: ping follows physical path for Mihomo and wg-quick, tunnel for Tailscale exit node without LAN access; panel does not display routerPingLatency; not published (low visible impact)

leads.summary: Several open network-status PRs independently modify the same route chooser and create the same new test filename
leads.consequence: Non-stacked #8866 and #8476 modify the same physical route/interface selection and both add a different test/shell.d/network-status-test.sh, so ordinary integration has unresolved conflicts in both script and test. #11302 (IPv6 route selection) and #7932 (separate route probe from multiple reachability targets) also conflict in the chooser; #11154 (TCP latency) merges its script but clashes over the same new test path. #8476's explicit --iface choice must take priority when combining, and #11302's IPv6-only fallback must remain reachable. #7932 renames internet_probe to route_probe: if its new declarations and this PR's display_route_json both survive, the latter's fallback passes an empty "$internet_probe" to ip route get; all hosts with no recognized main route become disconnected. #9809 also has a small adjacent-insertion merge conflict (max_link_freq vs display_route_json); #8683 adds IPv6 fields and conflicts at the verbose local declaration. Integrate these together rather than taking either side wholesale. GitHub reports each other's individual PR MERGEABLE against its base, which is not a guarantee that their pairwise merge works. Coordinate or combine the tests before merging together.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F3; #7932 internet_probe->route_probe rename verified by coordinator (triage/pr7932.diff) and by Opus in self-check; #8476/#9432 script conflicts per Opus conflicts.txt; published

leads.summary: Regression test cannot detect loss of the promised fallback to the existing probe route
leads.consequence: Every test scenario supplies a recognized Ethernet default and the last assertion explicitly rejects any route get call. Removing `ip -j route get` from display_route_json and returning [] instead leaves every assertion green, yet on hosts without a recognized physical main default the command now prints disconnected/empty details rather than falling back. Add a second stub case with [] or an unrecognized main route, assert the probe route and expected plain/verbose fields, and assert route get was called there. The test currently fails on merge-base for the positive path as intended, but does not protect the fallback.
leads.triage: corroborates Opus F5 (probe fallback mutant passes); published as Optional test improvement

limits: No real host interfaces, routes or services queried; all network process execution used review.py and synthetic stubs.

Physical route metric-order mutant intentionally not reported: the Linux IPv4 FIB inserts/dumps aliases in priority order (upstream/fib_trie.c:1194-1229,2259-2299), so feeding an arbitrarily reversed metric list to iproute2 is not representative.
Open-PR pairwise conflict markers were obtained from three-way file merges using each other PR's own merge-base and publicly fetched head file; conflicting merged scripts were not executed.

flags.fix: Use a name no checked PR uses, e.g. `network-status-physical-test.sh` or `network-status-route-test.sh` (free among the PRs I checked; not a search of every open PR).

flags.claim: A variant that accepts any type other than `tun` still passes all three assertions of the new test.
flags.fix: "A variant that accepts any non-empty type other than `tun` still passes all three assertions" (and say the tunnel check should still fall back to the probe route when the type is empty).

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** the change fixes the setup reported in #12069. With a Mihomo TUN on a policy-routing table and an Ethernet default in the main table, the status and `--verbose` output now describe the physical link instead of `Meta`:

| Stubbed scenario (interface names and addresses from the public issue #12069) | Merge base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Plain status | `ethernet  Meta` | `ethernet  enp0s13f0u1u4c2` |
| `--verbose` iface / ip / prefix / gateway | `Meta` / `198.18.0.1` / `30` / `198.18.0.2` | `enp0s13f0u1u4c2` / `10.0.11.181` / `24` / `10.0.11.1` |

Output is unchanged for a single Ethernet or Wi-Fi default, and for Ethernet plus Wi-Fi in either metric order. Hosts without NetworkManager, WWAN and IPv6-only hosts fall back to the old probe route as before. No scenario produced a nonzero exit or stderr output. The script and its call sites are unchanged between the merge base and the current `quattro` tip, and the PR merges cleanly onto it.

Three points are worth addressing: the Ethernet/Wi-Fi allow-list can pick the wrong link, the new address fallback can report the wrong address, and several open PRs rewrite the same code and add the same test file.

### A lower-priority Wi-Fi link wins over a bridge, bond or VLAN default

`display_route_json` walks the main-table defaults in metric order but accepts only devices whose `nmcli` type is `ethernet` or `wifi`. NetworkManager gives bond (300), team (350), VLAN (400), macvlan (410), bridge (425) and PPP (460) defaults a lower metric than Wi-Fi (600), so those preferred routes are skipped in favour of Wi-Fi.

Stubbed scenario: wired NIC in `br0` (metric 425, for example for VMs) and Wi-Fi connected as backup (metric 600):

| | Merge base | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Plain status | `ethernet  br0` | `wifi  HomeNet  78  5180.0` |
| `--verbose` iface / ip | `br0` / `192.168.1.20` | `wlan0` / `192.168.1.60` |

**Impact:** on such hosts the panel shows the Wi-Fi SSID, address, gateway and byte counters while traffic flows over the bridge. The merge base showed the correct device. The same allow-list also leaves a bond host behind a TUN unfixed (stubbed: it still shows `Meta`).

**Suggested change:** take the first main-table default whose device is not a tunnel (skip types such as `tun` and `wireguard`) instead of accepting only `ethernet`/`wifi`. A variant that accepts any non-empty type other than `tun` (so an empty type still falls back to the probe route) still passes all three assertions of the new test. Skipping routes whose `flags` contain `dead` would additionally keep a link-down Ethernet default from being chosen when `ignore_routes_with_linkdown` is set (the kernel then routes over Wi-Fi, while this PR keeps reporting the dead link; the merge base follows the kernel).

### The address fallback can report an address the kernel does not use

When the selected route has no `prefsrc`, the new fallback takes the first IPv4 address on the interface. That skips secondary addresses correctly. With real kernel routes in a namespace (synthetic addresses):

| Interface addresses, gateway | Kernel source | This PR's `--verbose` ip |
|---|---|---|
| `10.0.0.5/8` and `192.168.2.50/24` (both primary), gateway `192.168.2.1` | `192.168.2.50` | `10.0.0.5` |
| link-local `169.254.10.10/16` listed before `192.168.1.50/24` | `192.168.1.50` | `169.254.10.10` |

**Impact:** on such interfaces the panel and `--verbose` show an address that is not the one used for traffic. NetworkManager's DHCP default routes normally carry `src`, so this mostly affects static or manually added routes.

**Suggested change:** choose the global address whose subnet contains the gateway, and read `prefix` from the address actually displayed. That also fixes an older mismatch, present before this PR, where `prefix` comes from the first address even when `prefsrc` names a different one.

### Overlap with open PRs on the same script and test file

- #8866 ("Fix network panel behind VPN policy routes") fixes the same misreport in the same function with a different selection rule (first connected NM Wi-Fi/Ethernet device, then the lowest-metric main default). Each conflicts with the other in `bin/omarchy-network-status`, and both add `test/shell.d/network-status-test.sh`.
- #11154, #9432 and #8476 also add a `test/shell.d/network-status-test.sh`, so whichever merges first forces the others to rename or merge test files. #9432 and #8476 also conflict in the script.
- #11302, #9809, #8683, #12114 and #7932 conflict in `bin/omarchy-network-status`. #12114 contains its own "prefer Wi-Fi over tunnel" fix. #7932 renames `internet_probe` to `route_probe`; a resolution that keeps both changes must update the fallback in `display_route_json`, which still reads `$internet_probe`.

**Impact:** whichever of these PRs merges later needs rework in the script and, for the add/add cases, a renamed or merged test file.

**Suggested change:** name a distinct test file (for example `network-status-route-test.sh`; `network-status-tun-test.sh`, `-probe-` and `-ipv6-` are already used by #12114, #7932 and #11302) to avoid the add/add collisions, and link #8866 in the description so maintainers can choose between the two selection rules.

### Notes

**Behaviour change beyond TUN proxies:** full-tunnel VPNs that leave a physical default in the main table now show the physical link instead of the VPN interface. In stubbed scenarios this covers wg-quick (default in table 51820), OpenVPN `redirect-gateway def1`, and a VPN default in the main table at metric 50. This matches the expected behaviour in #12069, but the title, description and code comment mention only TUN routes. Stating it in the description would make the change easier to evaluate.

**Optional test improvement:** the test does not cover the promised fallback to the probe route. A mutant that replaces the `ip -j route get` fallback with an empty result still passes all three assertions. Also, its failure on the merge base comes from the `ip` stub rejecting the base's plain `ip route get` call (the base prints `disconnected`), not from observing `Meta`. A second case with no Ethernet/Wi-Fi main default that asserts the probe-route output, and a stub that also answers the plain `ip route get` form, would pin both.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** source review of the pinned head against the merge base and current `quattro` tip; iproute2 7.2.0, NetworkManager 1.58.1 and Linux kernel routing source. Behaviour comes from isolated runs of the merge-base and head scripts with stubbed `ip`, `nmcli` and `ping` (20 scenarios, plain and `--verbose`), plus namespace runs with real kernel routes for the link-down and address-fallback cases. The new test ran at the head, after a simulated merge onto the tip, and against the merge-base script; a mutation check ran against it. Not tested: live NetworkManager, Mihomo, WireGuard or OpenVPN; `nmcli` latency; shellcheck; the full `./test/shell` suite. Open-PR conflicts come from simulated merges.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
